description: Differentiation, limits, integration, complex numbers, series, Taylor approximation, matrices, linear systems, and eigenvalue methods for Level 1 Math I.
instructions: All main questions carry the same number of marks.
Show sufficient working to justify each answer.
Begin each main question on a new page.
label: Paper 1

questions.stem: This question concerns inverse hyperbolic differentiation, complex arithmetic, and logarithmic differentiation.
questions.title: Differentiation and algebraic form

parts.answer:
Use the chain rule with \(u=3x+2\). Since
\[
\frac{d}{du}\operatorname{arcosh}u=\frac{1}{\sqrt{u-1}\sqrt{u+1}},
\]
and \(du/dx=3\),
\[
f'(x)=\frac{3}{\sqrt{3x+1}\sqrt{3x+3}}.
\]
This derivative is valid where \(3x+2>1\), so \(x>-\frac{1}{3}\).
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Differentiate \(f(x)=\operatorname{arcosh}(3x+2)\), stating the interval where the derivative formula applies.

parts.answer:
First multiply the numerator:
\[
(4-3i)(2+i)=8+4i-6i-3i^2=11-2i.
\]
Divide by \(1-2i\) by multiplying by the conjugate:
\[
\frac{11-2i}{1-2i}\cdot\frac{1+2i}{1+2i}=\frac{(11-2i)(1+2i)}{1+4}.
\]
The numerator is
\[
11+22i-2i-4i^2=15+20i.
\]
Therefore
\[
\frac{(4-3i)(2+i)}{1-2i}=\frac{15+20i}{5}=3+4i.
\]
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle \frac{(4-3i)(2+i)}{1-2i}\) in the form \(a+bi\).

parts.answer:
Let
\[
y=(x^2+1)^4\sqrt{2x-1},
\]
where \(x>\frac{1}{2}\). Take logarithms:
\[
\ln y=4\ln(x^2+1)+\frac{1}{2}\ln(2x-1).
\]
Differentiate implicitly with respect to \(x\):
\[
\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}=4\cdot\frac{2x}{x^2+1}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{2x-1}.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{8x}{x^2+1}+\frac{1}{2x-1}.
\]
Multiplying by \(y\) gives
\[
\frac{dy}{dx}=(x^2+1)^4\sqrt{2x-1}\left(\frac{8x}{x^2+1}+\frac{1}{2x-1}\right).
\]
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use logarithmic differentiation to find \(\displaystyle \frac{dy}{dx}\) for \(y=(x^2+1)^4\sqrt{2x-1}\), where \(x>\frac{1}{2}\).

questions.stem: This question uses definite trigonometric integration, reduction formulae, and rational integration.
questions.title: Integration methods

parts.answer:
Use \(u=\cos x\), so \(du=-\sin x\,dx\). When \(x=0\), \(u=1\). When \(x=\frac{\pi}{3}\), \(u=\frac{1}{2}\). Hence
\[
\int_0^{\pi/3}\sin x\cos^3x\,dx=-\int_1^{1/2}u^3\,du=\int_{1/2}^{1}u^3\,du.
\]
Therefore
\[
\int_{1/2}^{1}u^3\,du=\left[\frac{u^4}{4}\right]_{1/2}^{1}=\frac{1}{4}\left(1-\frac{1}{16}\right)=\frac{15}{64}.
\]
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle \int_0^{\pi/3}\sin x\cos^3x\,dx\).

parts.answer:
Let
\[
I_n=\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^n x\,dx.
\]
For \(n\ge2\), write \(I_n=\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^{n-1}x\sin x\,dx\). Use integration by parts with \(u=\sin^{n-1}x\) and \(dv=\sin x\,dx\). Then \(du=(n-1)\sin^{n-2}x\cos x\,dx\) and \(v=-\cos x\). The boundary term is zero, so
\[
I_n=(n-1)\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^{n-2}x\cos^2x\,dx.
\]
Use \(\cos^2x=1-\sin^2x\):
\[
I_n=(n-1)(I_{n-2}-I_n).
\]
Hence
\[
nI_n=(n-1)I_{n-2},\qquad I_n=\frac{n-1}{n}I_{n-2}.
\]
Since \(I_0=\frac{\pi}{2}\),
\[
I_6=\frac{5}{6}I_4=\frac{5}{6}\cdot\frac{3}{4}I_2=\frac{5}{6}\cdot\frac{3}{4}\cdot\frac{1}{2}I_0=\frac{5\pi}{32}.
\]
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For \(I_n=\displaystyle \int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^n x\,dx\), derive the recurrence \(I_n=\frac{n-1}{n}I_{n-2}\) for \(n\ge2\), and use it to find \(I_6\).

parts.answer:
Divide the numerator by the denominator:
\[
\frac{2x^3+3x^2-5}{x^2+x-2}=2x+1+\frac{3x-3}{x^2+x-2}.
\]
Since \(x^2+x-2=(x-1)(x+2)\), the remainder term is
\[
\frac{3x-3}{(x-1)(x+2)}=\frac{3(x-1)}{(x-1)(x+2)}=\frac{3}{x+2},
\]
where the original integrand is defined. Thus
\[
\int\frac{2x^3+3x^2-5}{x^2+x-2}\,dx=\int\left(2x+1+\frac{3}{x+2}\right)dx.
\]
Therefore
\[
\int\frac{2x^3+3x^2-5}{x^2+x-2}\,dx=x^2+x+3\ln|x+2|+C.
\]
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle \int\frac{2x^3+3x^2-5}{x^2+x-2}\,dx\).

questions.stem: Evaluate each limit using an appropriate method, then solve the complex exponential equation.
questions.title: Limits and a complex exponential equation

parts.answer:
The expression has the form \(0/0\). Rationalise the numerator:
\[
\frac{\sqrt{4+x}-2}{x}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{4+x}+2}{\sqrt{4+x}+2}=\frac{4+x-4}{x(\sqrt{4+x}+2)}.
\]
For \(x\ne0\), this is
\[
\frac{1}{\sqrt{4+x}+2}.
\]
Taking the limit gives
\[
\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sqrt{4+x}-2}{x}=\frac{1}{2+2}=\frac{1}{4}.
\]
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle \lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sqrt{4+x}-2}{x}\).

parts.answer:
Use the standard expansion near zero,
\[
\cos u=1-\frac{u^2}{2}+O(u^4).
\]
With \(u=3x\),
\[
1-\cos(3x)=\frac{(3x)^2}{2}+O(x^4)=\frac{9x^2}{2}+O(x^4).
\]
Therefore
\[
\lim_{x\to0}\frac{1-\cos(3x)}{x^2}=\frac{9}{2}.
\]
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle \lim_{x\to0}\frac{1-\cos(3x)}{x^2}\).

parts.answer:
Let \(t=1/x\). As \(x\to0^+\), \(t\to\infty\). Then
\[
\lim_{x\to0^+}\frac{\sin(1/x)}{1/x}=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\sin t}{t}.
\]
For any \(t>0\), \(-1\le\sin t\le1\). Dividing by \(t\) gives
\[
-\frac{1}{t}\le\frac{\sin t}{t}\le\frac{1}{t}.
\]
As \(t\to\infty\), both bounds tend to \(0\). By the squeeze theorem,
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\sin t}{t}=0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\lim_{x\to0^+}\frac{\sin(1/x)}{1/x}=0.
\]
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle \lim_{x\to0^+}\frac{\sin(1/x)}{1/x}\) using a substitution and the squeeze theorem.

parts.answer:
Let \(z=x+iy\), where \(x,y\in\mathbb R\). Then
\[
e^{2z}=e^{2x}e^{2iy}.
\]
The right-hand side can be written as
\[
-9=9e^{i((2k+1)\pi)},\qquad k\in\mathbb Z.
\]
Equating moduli gives
\[
e^{2x}=9,\qquad 2x=\ln9,\qquad x=\ln3.
\]
Equating arguments gives
\[
2y=(2k+1)\pi,\qquad y=\frac{(2k+1)\pi}{2}.
\]
Therefore all solutions are
\[
z=\ln3+i\frac{(2k+1)\pi}{2},\qquad k\in\mathbb Z.
\]
parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Find all complex solutions of \(e^{2z}=-9\).

questions.stem: This question concerns convergence tests for numerical series and a power series.
questions.title: Convergence and intervals

parts.answer:
For \(n\ge1\), compare with \(1/n^2\). Since
\[
0<\frac{n+2}{n^3+1}\le\frac{3n}{n^3}=\frac{3}{n^2},
\]
and the \(p\)-series
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{3}{n^2}
\]
converges, the comparison test shows that
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{n+2}{n^3+1}
\]
converges.
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use a comparison test to determine whether \(\displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{n+2}{n^3+1}\) converges.

parts.answer:
Let
\[
a_n=\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{\sqrt n+1}.
\]
The positive magnitudes
\[
b_n=\frac{1}{\sqrt n+1}
\]
decrease to zero, so the alternating series test shows that \(\sum a_n\) converges. For absolute convergence, consider
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{\sqrt n+1}.
\]
For \(n\ge1\), \(\sqrt n+1\le2\sqrt n\), so
\[
\frac{1}{\sqrt n+1}\ge\frac{1}{2\sqrt n}.
\]
The series \(\sum 1/(2\sqrt n)\) diverges because it is a \(p\)-series with \(p=\frac{1}{2}\). Hence the absolute series diverges. Therefore the original series is conditionally convergent.
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Determine whether \(\displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{\sqrt n+1}\) converges absolutely, converges conditionally, or diverges.

parts.answer:
Let
\[
a_n(x)=\frac{(x+1)^n}{3^n\sqrt{n}}.
\]
Use the root test on absolute values:
\[
\sqrt[n]{|a_n(x)|}=\sqrt[n]{\frac{|x+1|^n}{3^n\sqrt{n}}}=\frac{|x+1|}{3}\,n^{-1/2n}.
\]
As \(n\to\infty\), \(n^{-1/2n}=e^{-\frac{\ln n}{2n}}\to e^0=1\). Thus
\[
L=\frac{|x+1|}{3}.
\]
The series converges absolutely when \(L<1\), so \(|x+1|<3\) or \(-4<x<2\). At \(x=2\), the series becomes
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}},
\]
which is a \(p\)-series with \(p=\frac{1}{2}\le1\), so it diverges. At \(x=-4\), the series becomes
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^n}{\sqrt{n}},
\]
which converges by the alternating series test. Therefore the interval of convergence is
\[
[-4,2).
\]
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use the root test to find the interval of convergence of \(\displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(x+1)^n}{3^n\sqrt{n}}\), classifying both endpoints.

questions.section: Section E: Taylor Series and Matrices
questions.stem: This question combines Taylor approximation with orthogonal and symmetric matrix structure.
questions.title: Taylor bounds and orthogonal matrices

parts.answer:
For \(f(x)=e^{-x}\), the derivatives alternate in sign, and
\[
f^{(k)}(0)=(-1)^k.
\]
The cubic Taylor polynomial about \(0\) is
\[
P_3(x)=1-x+\frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{x^3}{6}.
\]
At \(x=0.4\),
\[
P_3(0.4)=1-0.4+\frac{0.4^2}{2}-\frac{0.4^3}{6}=0.669333\ldots .
\]
For a Lagrange remainder bound on \([0,0.4]\), \(|f^{(4)}(x)|=e^{-x}\le1\). Thus
\[
|R_3(0.4)|\le\frac{1}{4!}(0.4)^4=\frac{0.0256}{24}=0.001066\ldots .
\]
Because the Taylor series for \(e^{-0.4}\) is alternating with decreasing term sizes, the alternating-series remainder is bounded by the next term:
\[
|R_3(0.4)|\le\frac{0.4^4}{4!}=0.001066\ldots .
\]
So \(e^{-0.4}\approx0.669333\), with error at most about \(0.00107\) by either bound.
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the cubic Taylor polynomial for \(e^{-x}\) about \(0\), use it to approximate \(e^{-0.4}\), and give both a Lagrange remainder bound and an alternating-series remainder bound.

parts.answer:
Let
\[
Q=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\-b&a\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The columns are
\[
\mathbf q_1=\begin{pmatrix}a\\-b\end{pmatrix},\qquad \mathbf q_2=\begin{pmatrix}b\\a\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For \(Q\) to be orthogonal, its columns must be orthonormal. Their squared lengths are
\[
\|\mathbf q_1\|^2=a^2+b^2,\qquad \|\mathbf q_2\|^2=a^2+b^2,
\]
and their dot product is
\[
\mathbf q_1\cdot\mathbf q_2=ab-ba=0.
\]
Thus the columns are orthonormal exactly when
\[
a^2+b^2=1.
\]
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the condition on real numbers \(a\) and \(b\) for \(Q=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\-b&a\end{pmatrix}\) to be orthogonal.

parts.answer:
For any orthogonal matrix \(Q\),
\[
Q^TQ=I.
\]
Multiplying by \(Q^{-1}\) is not needed: the equation already says that \(Q^T\) is a left inverse for \(Q\). For square matrices, a left inverse is the inverse, so
\[
Q^{-1}=Q^T.
\]
For this matrix,
\[
Q^{-1}=Q^T=\begin{pmatrix}a&-b\\b&a\end{pmatrix}.
\]
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: If \(Q\) is orthogonal, state \(Q^{-1}\) in terms of \(Q^T\), and give the inverse of the matrix in part (b).

parts.answer:
Let \(A\) be symmetric and orthogonal, and suppose \(A\mathbf v=\lambda\mathbf v\) for a non-zero real vector \(\mathbf v\). Since \(A\) is orthogonal, it preserves lengths:
\[
\|A\mathbf v\|=\|\mathbf v\|.
\]
Using the eigenvalue equation,
\[
\|A\mathbf v\|=\|\lambda\mathbf v\|=|\lambda|\|\mathbf v\|.
\]
Because \(\mathbf v\ne\mathbf0\), \(\|\mathbf v\|\ne0\), so
\[
|\lambda|=1.
\]
A real symmetric matrix has real eigenvalues, hence \(\lambda=1\) or \(\lambda=-1\). Therefore every eigenvalue of a real symmetric orthogonal matrix is restricted to \(\pm1\).
parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Prove that every eigenvalue of a real symmetric orthogonal matrix is either \(1\) or \(-1\).

questions.stem:
Consider the parameter-dependent linear system
\[
\begin{aligned}
x+2y-z&=1,\\
3x+5y+z&=4,\\
2x+(a+4)y+az&=b.
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.title: A parameter-dependent linear system

parts.answer:
Use the augmented matrix
\[
\left(\begin{array}{ccc|c}1&2&-1&1\\3&5&1&4\\2&a+4&a&b\end{array}\right).
\]
Apply \(R_2\leftarrow R_2-3R_1\) and \(R_3\leftarrow R_3-2R_1\):
\[
\left(\begin{array}{ccc|c}1&2&-1&1\\0&-1&4&1\\0&a&a+2&b-2\end{array}\right).
\]
The lower \(2\times2\) coefficient block has determinant
\[
(-1)(a+2)-4a=-5a-2.
\]
Thus the coefficient matrix is invertible exactly when
\[
-5a-2\ne0,\qquad a\ne-\frac{2}{5}.
\]
So the system has a unique solution for \(a\ne-\frac{2}{5}\).
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the values of \(a\) for which the system has a unique solution.

parts.answer:
When \(a=-\frac{2}{5}\), the reduced augmented matrix from part (a) becomes
\[
\left(\begin{array}{ccc|c}1&2&-1&1\\0&-1&4&1\\0&-\frac{2}{5}&\frac{8}{5}&b-2\end{array}\right).
\]
The third coefficient row is \(\frac{2}{5}\) times the second coefficient row, since
\[
\frac{2}{5}(0,-1,4)=\left(0,-\frac{2}{5},\frac{8}{5}\right).
\]
For consistency, the right-hand side must have the same factor:
\[
b-2=\frac{2}{5}\cdot1=\frac{2}{5}.
\]
Therefore
\[
b=\frac{12}{5}.
\]
If \(a=-\frac{2}{5}\) and \(b=\frac{12}{5}\), there are infinitely many solutions. If \(a=-\frac{2}{5}\) and \(b\ne\frac{12}{5}\), the system is inconsistent and has no solution.
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Classify the non-unique cases as no solution or infinitely many solutions.

parts.answer:
For the associated homogeneous system in the singular case, take \(a=-\frac{2}{5}\). The reduced coefficient equations are
\[
x+2y-z=0,\qquad -y+4z=0.
\]
Let \(z=t\). Then
\[
y=4t.
\]
Substitute into the first equation:
\[
x+2(4t)-t=0,\qquad x=-7t.
\]
Hence the non-zero homogeneous solutions are
\[
\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}=t\begin{pmatrix}-7\\4\\1\end{pmatrix},\qquad t\in\mathbb R,\ t\ne0.
\]
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: For the singular value of \(a\), solve the associated homogeneous system.

parts.answer:
Set \(a=0\) and \(b=3\). The reduced augmented matrix from part (a) is
\[
\left(\begin{array}{ccc|c}1&2&-1&1\\0&-1&4&1\\0&0&2&1\end{array}\right).
\]
The last row gives
\[
2z=1,\qquad z=\frac{1}{2}.
\]
The second row gives
\[
-y+4z=1,\qquad y=4\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)-1=1.
\]
The first row gives
\[
x+2(1)-\frac{1}{2}=1,\qquad x=-\frac{1}{2}.
\]
Therefore, when \(a=0\) and \(b=3\),
\[
(x,y,z)=\left(-\frac{1}{2},1,\frac{1}{2}\right).
\]
parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Solve the system for \(a=0\) and \(b=3\).

questions.section: Section G: Eigenvalues and Matrix Structure
questions.title: Diagonalisation and commuting matrices

parts.answer:
Compute the action of \(A\) on each vector:
\[
A\mathbf v_1=\begin{pmatrix}2\\0\\0\end{pmatrix}=2\mathbf v_1,
\]
\[
A\mathbf v_2=\begin{pmatrix}0\\4\\4\end{pmatrix}=4\mathbf v_2,
\]
\[
A\mathbf v_3=\begin{pmatrix}0\\2\\-2\end{pmatrix}=2\mathbf v_3.
\]
Thus the eigenvalues corresponding to \(\mathbf v_1,\mathbf v_2,\mathbf v_3\) are respectively
\[
2,\quad 4,\quad 2.
\]
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Verify that the supplied vectors are eigenvectors of \(A\), and state the corresponding eigenvalues.

parts.answer:
Use the eigenvectors as columns of \(P\):
\[
P=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&1\\0&1&-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The matching diagonal matrix is
\[
D_A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0&0\\0&4&0\\0&0&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Since the columns of \(P\) are eigenvectors of \(A\),
\[
AP=PD_A.
\]
The determinant of \(P\) is
\[
\det P=1\det\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}=-2\ne0.
\]
Therefore \(P\) is invertible and
\[
A=PD_AP^{-1}.
\]
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Construct matrices \(P\) and \(D_A\) such that \(A=PD_AP^{-1}\), and justify that the diagonalisation is valid.

parts.answer:
The same vectors are also eigenvectors of \(B\):
\[
B\mathbf v_1=5\mathbf v_1,\qquad B\mathbf v_2=3\mathbf v_2,\qquad B\mathbf v_3=-\mathbf v_3.
\]
Hence
\[
B=PD_BP^{-1},\qquad D_B=\begin{pmatrix}5&0&0\\0&3&0\\0&0&-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Now
\[
AB=(PD_AP^{-1})(PD_BP^{-1})=PD_AD_BP^{-1},
\]
and
\[
BA=(PD_BP^{-1})(PD_AP^{-1})=PD_BD_AP^{-1}.
\]
Diagonal matrices commute, so \(D_AD_B=D_BD_A\). Therefore
\[
AB=BA.
\]
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Show, using diagonal form, that \(A\) and \(B\) commute.

parts.answer:
Let \(A\) and \(B\) be square matrices with \(AB=BA\). Suppose \(\mathbf v\) lies in the eigenspace of \(A\) for eigenvalue \(\lambda\). Then
\[
A\mathbf v=\lambda\mathbf v.
\]
Apply \(A\) to \(B\mathbf v\):
\[
A(B\mathbf v)=(AB)\mathbf v.
\]
Since \(AB=BA\),
\[
(AB)\mathbf v=(BA)\mathbf v=B(A\mathbf v).
\]
Using \(A\mathbf v=\lambda\mathbf v\),
\[
B(A\mathbf v)=B(\lambda\mathbf v)=\lambda B\mathbf v.
\]
Thus
\[
A(B\mathbf v)=\lambda B\mathbf v.
\]
So \(B\mathbf v\) is either the zero vector or another vector in the same eigenspace of \(A\). Therefore commuting maps preserve eigenspaces.
parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Prove that if square matrices \(A\) and \(B\) commute, then \(B\) maps each eigenspace of \(A\) into itself.
